rows.stem:
The following diagram shows the electrolytic refining of copper :

Which of the following statements is **incorrect** description of the process ?

options.label: A
options.text: The impure metal from the anode dissolves into the electrolyte.

options.label: B
options.text: The pure metal from the electrolyte is deposited on the cathode.

options.label: C
options.text: Insoluble impurities settle down at the bottom of the anode.

options.label: D
options.text: On passing the current through the electrolyte, the pure metal from the anode dissolves into the electrolyte.

rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - an electrolytic tank with the cathode (negative) and anode (positive) plates dipping in acidified copper sulphate solution, Cu2+ ions drawn moving between them and anode mud at the bottom; every option is a text statement the student can judge without it. Page idx 10.
rows.solution:
In electrolytic refining, the impure metal is the anode, a thin strip of pure metal is the cathode, and a solution of a salt of the metal (here acidified copper sulphate) is the electrolyte. When the current is passed, the pure metal from the anode dissolves into the electrolyte, and an equivalent amount of pure metal from the electrolyte is deposited on the cathode. The soluble impurities go into the solution, and the insoluble impurities settle down at the bottom of the anode as anode mud.

So the statements about deposition on the cathode, the settling of insoluble impurities and the pure metal dissolving from the anode are all correct; the last is NCERT's own sentence. Only the metal itself dissolves from the impure anode; its insoluble impurities do not go into the electrolyte but collect as anode mud. Saying that the impure metal dissolves is therefore the incorrect description.

This is option (A) The impure metal from the anode dissolves into the electrolyte.

rows.stem: Which of the following metals **do not** corrode in moist air ?
rows.solution:
Gold is a very unreactive (noble) metal, so it does not react with the oxygen, moisture or other gases of the air and keeps its shine. Copper slowly gets a green coating of basic copper carbonate in moist air, iron rusts, and silver turns black because it reacts with sulphur compounds in the air.

This is option (C) Gold.

rows.stem: If the current I through a resistor is increased by 100% (at constant temperature), the increase in power dissipated will be
rows.solution:
At constant temperature the resistance R stays the same, and \(P = I^2R\).

If the current increases by 100%, it becomes \(2I\), so the new power is \((2I)^2R = 4I^2R = 4P\).

The increase is \(4P - P = 3P\), that is, 300% of the original power.

This is option (C) 300%.

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Left atrium receives oxygenated blood from pulmonary vein.

**Reason (R) :** Right atrium transfers deoxygenated blood to the right ventricle, which pumps it to the lungs for oxygenation.
rows.context:
Q. Nos. 17 to 20 are Assertion – Reason based questions.

These consist of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer these questions selecting the appropriate option given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

rows.solution:
The pulmonary veins bring oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium, so the Assertion is true.

The right atrium receives deoxygenated blood from the body and passes it to the right ventricle, which pumps it to the lungs for oxygenation. So the Reason is true. But it describes the right side of the heart and says nothing about why the left atrium receives oxygenated blood, so it does not explain the Assertion.

Both statements are true but the Reason does not explain the Assertion, which is option (B).

rows.stem: A plant hormone helps in bending of stem towards light. Name the hormone and explain how is the movement achieved.
rows.solution:
The hormone is auxin.

Auxin is synthesised at the tip of the shoot. When light falls on the plant from one side, auxin diffuses towards the shady side of the shoot. The higher concentration of auxin there stimulates the cells on the shady side to grow longer than the cells on the lighted side, so the shoot bends towards the light (phototropism).

rows.stem: Write the constituents of solder alloy. Which property of solder makes it suitable for welding electrical wires ?
rows.solution:
Solder is an alloy of lead and tin (Pb and Sn).

It has a low melting point, so it melts easily and can be used to join (weld) electrical wires together.

rows.stem: Why is damage to the ozone layer a cause for concern ? What steps are being taken to limit this damage ?
rows.solution:
The ozone layer in the upper atmosphere shields the surface of the earth from the ultraviolet (UV) radiation of the sun. If it is damaged, more UV radiation reaches the earth, and this is harmful: it causes skin cancer in human beings (and damages the eyes and the immune system).

Steps being taken to limit the damage:

1. Minimising the use of chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), which are the main cause of ozone depletion, in refrigerants and fire extinguishers.

2. In 1987 the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) forged an agreement to freeze CFC production at 1986 levels; manufacturing companies are now required to make CFC-free refrigerators.

rows.subtopic: Common Salt and Chemicals from It
rows.stem:
A chemical compound X is used in glass, soap and paper industries. On treatment with ethanoic acid, it forms salt, water and carbon dioxide.

(a) Identify X.

(b) How is this compound obtained from brine ? Write the equations involved.

(c) State the number of molecules of water of crystallization present in compound X.
rows.solution:
(a) X is washing soda, sodium carbonate decahydrate, \(\mathrm{Na_2CO_3 \cdot 10H_2O}\). It is used in the glass, soap and paper industries, and with ethanoic acid it gives a salt (sodium ethanoate), water and carbon dioxide:

\(\mathrm{Na_2CO_3 + 2CH_3COOH \rightarrow 2CH_3COONa + H_2O + CO_2}\)

(b) Ammonia and carbon dioxide are passed through brine (a concentrated solution of sodium chloride). Sodium hydrogen carbonate is formed, which is only slightly soluble and separates out:

\(\mathrm{NaCl + H_2O + CO_2 + NH_3 \rightarrow NH_4Cl + NaHCO_3}\)

On heating, sodium hydrogen carbonate gives sodium carbonate:

\(\mathrm{2NaHCO_3 \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} Na_2CO_3 + H_2O + CO_2}\)

Sodium carbonate is then recrystallised from water to give washing soda:

\(\mathrm{Na_2CO_3 + 10H_2O \rightarrow Na_2CO_3 \cdot 10H_2O}\)

(c) Ten molecules of water of crystallisation are present in one formula unit of washing soda.

rows.stem:
A student wants to project the image of a candle flame on a screen 60 cm in front of a mirror by keeping the candle at a distance of 15 cm from its pole.

(a) Name the type of mirror used.

(b) Also calculate :

(i) Magnification of the image produced

(ii) Distance between object and its image

(c) Draw a ray diagram to show the image formation.
rows.solution:
(a) The image is formed on a screen, so it is real. A real image is formed only by a concave (converging) mirror, so the mirror is concave.

(b) The candle and the screen are both in front of the mirror, so \(u = -15\) cm and \(v = -60\) cm.

(i) \(m = -\dfrac{v}{u} = -\dfrac{(-60)}{(-15)} = -4\)

The image is real, inverted and four times the size of the flame.

(ii) The object is 15 cm and the image 60 cm from the mirror, on the same side, so the distance between them is \(60 - 15 = 45\) cm.

(For the diagram, the focal length follows from the mirror formula: \(\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{u} = -\dfrac{1}{60} - \dfrac{1}{15} = -\dfrac{5}{60}\), so \(f = -12\) cm and the centre of curvature C is 24 cm from the pole. The candle at 15 cm is therefore between F and C.)

(c) Draw a concave mirror with its principal axis, and mark F and C in front of it. Place the object AB between F and C. A ray from A parallel to the principal axis is reflected through F. A ray from A passing through F is reflected parallel to the principal axis. The two reflected rays meet at A' below the axis, beyond C. Draw A'B' perpendicular to the axis: the image is beyond C, real, inverted and enlarged. Draw arrows on the rays.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.subtopic: Defects of Vision and their Correction
rows.stem: A person cannot see distinctly the object placed beyond 5 m from his eyes. Name the defect of vision the person is suffering from. Draw a ray diagram to illustrate this defect. List its two possible causes. Name the lens used for the correction of this defect.
rows.solution:
The person cannot see distant objects clearly: the far point of his eye is at 5 m instead of infinity. The defect is myopia (short-sightedness).

Diagram: draw an eyeball with its lens. Parallel rays from a distant object enter the eye and are converged by the eye lens to a point in front of the retina, so the image of the distant object is formed in front of the retina and is blurred. Mark the far point O of the myopic eye in front of the eye, with the rays from O shown focusing on the retina.

Two possible causes:

1. Excessive curvature of the eye lens.

2. Elongation of the eyeball.

The defect is corrected by a concave (diverging) lens of suitable power.

rows.stem:
(a) Mention the role of the following organs of human male reproductive system :

(i) Testis

(ii) Scrotum

(iii) Vas-deferens

(iv) Seminal vesicle

(b) What is Placenta ? State its function in a human female.
rows.solution:
(a) (i) Testis: produces the male gametes, the sperms, and the male hormone testosterone.

(ii) Scrotum: holds the testes outside the abdominal cavity, where the temperature is lower than the body temperature; this lower, optimal temperature is needed for the formation of sperms.

(iii) Vas deferens: carries the sperms from the testis to the urethra.

(iv) Seminal vesicle: secretes a fluid which provides nutrition to the sperms and a fluid medium that makes their transport easier.

(b) The placenta is a special disc-shaped tissue embedded in the wall of the uterus, which connects the mother to the embryo. It has villi on the embryo's side and blood spaces on the mother's side, which surround the villi, so it provides a large surface area.

Function: it allows the exchange of materials between the mother and the embryo (foetus). Glucose, oxygen and other nutrients pass from the mother's blood to the embryo, and the wastes produced by the embryo, such as carbon dioxide, are removed by transferring them into the mother's blood.
